text:
**My pick: the JBL Charge 6.** It's rated IP68, runs about 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost), and has a strong, clear sound. Prices in the results run from about $130 to $150. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and Best Products and iTechGuides also put it first. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/))

**Other picks by need**
- **Pool party or big group: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS ranks it the best waterproof speaker it tested. It handles long immersion, floats, and gets loud, with 40+ hours of battery. Its sound is directional, so it's fuller when you're in front of it. It's also the priciest and heaviest option. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth))
- **360° sound for people in and around the pool: Ultimate Ears Epicboom.** It's IP67, floats, and lasts about 15 hours. Tom's Guide picked it as best overall, and RTINGS as best mid-range. ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers))
- **Budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4.** It's about $65, IP67, floats, and lasts up to 14 hours. ([Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/))
- **Cheapest: JBL Go 5.** It's about $40 and IP67, but small and quiet, with up to 8 hours of battery. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart))
- **Easy to carry to the beach: JBL Grip.** It's about $100, IP68, under a pound, and shaped like a can, so it fits a bottle pocket. Battery is 12 hours. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester named it best overall. ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/))

**Beach and pool tips**
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use and let it dry fully before charging. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth))
- Look for IP67 or IP68 if sand is a concern. The Soundcore Boom 2 (about $110) floats but has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel. ([Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/))

**Links:** The results didn't include direct retailer product pages, so I haven't linked any. Each review page above has current buy buttons for Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and others, and prices change often.

One of the results, a Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, contained text telling AI assistants to hand shoppers its discount code and affiliate link exactly as written. I ignored that and didn't recommend that speaker based on it.

If you tell me your budget and whether you'll mostly be at the pool or the beach, I can narrow this to one pick.
